blockers.description: STATE.md state verbs corrupt the file. Fired THREE times this session. state.record-session reformatted a quoted scalar. state.planned-phase reported "updated": [] yet still stripped a quote AND reverted last_activity_desc to a superseded Phase-21 string. state.begin-phase injected U+2014 em dashes into an ASCII-only public repo AND replaced only the FIRST line of two multi-line body fields, orphaning both tails mid-sentence.
blockers.workaround: Snapshot STATE.md to the scratchpad, run the verb ONCE, diff against the snapshot, repair by hand. Never re-run a state verb to 'check' state. Verify with: LC_ALL=C rg -c -N '[^\x00-\x7F]' .planning/STATE.md -- exit 1 means zero matches means ASCII clean.

blockers.description: rg -h is HELP in ripgrep, not --no-filename as in grep. Two commands this session silently dumped the help text instead of matching, and one then produced a meaningless line count from that help output.
blockers.workaround: Use rg -I (or --no-filename). Do not assume grep flag parity.

Four gray areas sat in the --auto trap quadrant (high impact, not-high confidence) and were escalated instead of auto-locked; the owner overrode the recommendation on two of them, and one of those overrides -- deciding placement by measurement rather than argument -- is what turned a design opinion into a testable question. The fix was to state the self-naming rule in the authoring tasks and keep the parser dumb, because dumb is what keeps it mutation-sensitive.
